points.t: ‘Urticaria’ where each wheal lasts more than 24 hours, burns or hurts, and leaves bruising or brown staining.
Immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis; low C3/C4 and anti-C1q in the hypocomplementaemic form.
Mark a wheal to time it; check complement, ESR/CRP, urine, ANA; refer for biopsy; antihistamines help itch but not the vasculitis.
HUVS with lupus, kidney, lung (COPD-like) or eye involvement.

points: **drugs** (ACE-i, penicillins, sulfonamides, fluoxetine, cimetidine, diltiazem, thiazides, potassium iodide, NSAIDs, glatiramer; also TNF inhibitors)
**paraproteins** (IgM — **Schnitzler syndrome** — and IgA gammopathy), mixed cryoglobulinaemia
(H&E + DIF, ideally a lesion <48 h old) — essential, because the clinical overlap with urticaria is large.

items.t: Wheals with joint pain, fever, abdominal pain, breathlessness or abnormal urine: suspect **systemic (hypocomplementaemic) disease**, refer urgently.

pearls.t: "**Wheals that last more than a day, burn, and leave a bruise = biopsy.**"
Ask patients to **circle a wheal with a pen** and photograph it daily — it documents duration (cheap, effective).
